prompt:
A page from a travel sketchbook: a loose but skilful graphite pencil sketch of a harbour scene, drawn by hand on plain smooth white drawing paper, used as a background for a 2D narrative game.

Technique: soft graphite pencil (2B to 4B). Confident, slightly wobbly hand-drawn contour lines that sometimes overshoot at the corners and are drawn twice in places, a few visible construction lines (a light horizon line, the vertical axis of the lighthouse). Shading is built from pencil hatching only: groups of parallel diagonal strokes, cross-hatching in the darkest areas (under the jetty, the shadow side of the cottage and of the rocks, the hulls of the boats), a few soft graphite smudges rubbed with a finger, and eraser marks where light was lifted out of the graphite (around the lit window, the lantern and the lighthouse lamp, a pale streak of light on the water), plus a few faint ghost lines of an earlier attempt that was erased. Strokes must stay bold and clearly readable at screen size: contour lines about 3 to 4 pixels wide, hatching strokes clearly separated with white paper between them (about 6 to 9 pixels apart), never a fine grey mush, never smooth photographic tonal gradients. Mostly grey graphite only; just a few touches of coloured pencil hatched on top: red on the band of the lighthouse, warm yellow on the lit window and the lantern glass, a few strokes of orange along the band of light at the horizon. The paper stays white between the strokes; large parts of the sky and of the calm water are blank white paper with only a few horizontal strokes, low clouds drawn as loose outlines with a little hatching underneath, the first stars as tiny pencil crosses.

Composition: a wide sketch across the middle of the sheet. It spans the full width but only about the middle 60 percent of the height; above and below it there is blank white paper, and its upper and lower edges are loose and unfinished, the hatching fading out into the paper. Side view of the harbour from the quay, eye level of a small figure. The stone quay in the front runs along the bottom of the sketch and is close to the viewer: its paving is drawn with a few lines in perspective, and it is open and empty from the left edge to the middle of the picture. A badger character, added later as a separate sprite, will stand on this front quay and will be about 40 percent of the height of the sketch tall; draw everything at that scale: the barrels about a third of the height of the sketch, the barrels, the stack of crates and the coil of rope on the right part of the front quay. The iron lantern on its wooden post stands on the quay a little left of the centre and rises well above the horizon, the lantern itself in front of the sky. The cottage stands on the left at the back of the quay, its chimney in front of open sky. The wooden jetty with the two moored boats is in the middle distance, the lighthouse on its rocky headland on the right at about 85 percent of the width, its top well below the upper edge of the sketch.

Effects that are animated separately in the game must not be drawn: the lighthouse lamp is only a small lit spot without any beam or rays, the lantern without rays or glow lines, no smoke from the chimney, no birds in the sky.

Not a photograph, not a 3D render, not a painting, not a watercolour, not an ink drawing, not an engraving, not a comic with black outlines, not a finished polished illustration, not a postcard. No notebook lines, no grid, no paper texture, no torn edges, no frame or border, no hands, no pencils, no table, no visible sketchbook binding: only the drawing on white paper.

Location: the small harbour of Lornholm, a fictional island in a northern sea, at dusk. A stone quay with a short wooden jetty runs along the lower third of the picture. Two small wooden fishing boats are moored at the jetty. On a rocky headland on the right stands a white lighthouse with one red band, its lamp lit. On the left a small stone harbour-master's cottage with a lit window and a smoking chimney. On the quay: two barrels, a stack of crates, a coil of rope and an iron lantern on a wooden post. Calm sea, low clouds, a band of orange light at the horizon, the first stars.

Leave the quay in the foreground free of characters: it is a game background, characters are added later as separate sprites.

No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

Image format: landscape 3:2.

Sprite sheet for a 2D side-view narrative game: ten small figures of the same character, drawn as a loose graphite pencil sketch from a travel sketchbook, each figure about 250 pixels tall. The first reference image gives the exact layout and the exact poses: ten figures in two rows of five, all at the same scale, the feet of each row on the same baseline. Figures one to eight (in reading order) are a walk cycle to the right in strict side view; figure nine stands still in side view, both feet flat on the ground; figure ten has turned three-quarters towards the viewer. Copy every pose, the positions of both legs and feet, the arms, the parcel and the satchel, and the place of each figure exactly from the first reference; only the drawing changes. The first reference is a plain 3D render: take only the layout and the poses from it, never its smooth shading or its plastic 3D look. The second reference image only shows the costume and the proportions of the character: do not copy its painting style, its colours or its three-view layout. The third reference image is the game background, a pencil sketch: draw the figures with exactly the same pencil technique, the same absolute stroke width and the same spacing of the hatching as in the third reference, so the figures sit in that drawing as if sketched by the same hand on the same page.

Technique: soft graphite pencil (2B to 4B) on plain white paper. Confident, slightly wobbly hand-drawn contour lines around the figure and around every costume part, about 3 pixels wide, overshooting a little at some corners; shading only from pencil hatching: groups of parallel diagonal strokes that follow the round forms, cross-hatching in the darkest parts, clearly separated strokes with white paper between them (about 5 to 7 pixels apart), never a grey mush, never smooth tonal gradients, no airbrush. Light from the upper left. The colours of the costume become graphite tone values: the dark fur of the body, arms and legs and the dark face stripes in dense cross-hatching, the broad white face stripe and the light belly as bare white paper inside a contour line, the cream shirt white with a few strokes in the shadow, the dark green cap and vest in medium hatching, the satchel dark, the parcel light with its string. The only colour on the figure: the long knitted scarf is hatched in red coloured pencil, with its knitted ribs and fringe drawn as short strokes. Keep the face readable at this size: a small dark eye with a tiny white highlight, a dark nose, a slight smile, the broad white stripe clearly separated from the dark stripe. Not a painting, not a cartoon with black ink outlines, not a 3D render, not an engraving.

The badger courier: an original mascot character, a stout, short-legged badger with a broad black-and-white striped face, wearing a dark green peaked cap with a brass button, a dark green vest with pockets over a cream shirt with rolled-up sleeves, a long red knitted scarf, a brown leather satchel on a shoulder strap, and a brown paper parcel tied with string under one arm.

Each figure isolated on a fully transparent background; inside the figure the white paper between the strokes is opaque white. Clear empty space between the figures; no ground, no cast shadow, no frame borders, nothing cut off at the edge of the sheet.

No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

Image format: landscape 3:2.
